shelfmark: UTO Sinai Syriac NF M 3, SPP No. 71

note: Melkite Estrangela | Neat and fairly regular; some serto features. The script is quite similar to that of Tropologion B, but usually rather neater

Sometimes part of a margin is present, top, right, left, or bottom (occasionally a combination of two of these). Blank spaces within or between lines probably had rubrics in different ink, which have left no trace in any of the images

Usually only parts of lines are preserved, and only where the name of a saint is legible has it been possible to identify a specific underlying Greek canon. In such cases, it is clear that the translation is very free, and also different from that of the same canon which happens to be preserved in British Library manuscripts

program.description: Imaged and studied as part of the Sinai Palimpsests Project (2011–2016), a collaboration between St. Catherine’s Monastery of the Sinai, the Early Manuscripts Electronic Library, and UCLA Library, funded by the Arcadia Fund and the Ahmanson Foundation. The project used multispectral imaging and scholarly analysis to recover and document erased and obscured texts in palimpsest manuscripts from the monastery’s collection.
